what: Studies of the seven edges on the train pool: filled trades that are not flagged, net R after costs. The exam pool is never read. Research proposes; the mentor decides.

preregistration.statement: Families, buckets, split, minimum sample, correction and pass rule were fixed in the code before any condition result was computed. Nothing was tuned after a run.

families.title: Stop size, reward to risk and side

buckets.rule: One bucket a listed value of a categorical key, one for a yes / no key, two for a numeric key (the lowest and the highest third, cut on the discovery part only). Rows where the key is unknown are left out.

split.by: the first 70 % of an edge's trades in signal-time order, by count; confirmation is the rest
split.baseline: baselines use the period cut of eval.json: 70 % of the way from the first order to the last, by time

passRule: An edge runs condition studies only if its confirmation part holds at least 40 trades; a smaller edge gets one entry saying so and no test.

A condition is tested only when the bucket and the rest each hold at least 20 trades in the discovery part and in the confirmation part. Otherwise: inconclusive, too few trades, and it is not counted as a test.
The measure is net R a trade inside the bucket minus outside it, with a two-sided Welch t, in each part.
Discovery passes at |t| >= 2. A condition that does not pass discovery is inconclusive.

A condition that passes discovery is: rejected when the confirmation difference has the opposite sign; in-sample when the sign holds but the confirmation |t| is under 2; out-of-sample when the sign holds and the confirmation |t| is at least 2.
validated = out-of-sample AND the discovery p-value survives Benjamini-Hochberg at 10 % across every discovery test of the run.
Baseline, regime, book and policy studies are descriptions of the train pool. They carry the label in-sample and are never called an edge.
lessonRule: A draft lesson is written only for a condition that reached out-of-sample or validated.
Bucket worse than the rest: the draft says WAIT when the condition holds. Bucket better than the rest: the draft says TAKE.

Every draft is inactive, carries its evidence (n, net R a trade and t in both parts) and its study id, and says so when the bucket still made money (a WAIT then gives up profit) or still lost money (better than the rest is not good).

pool.note: exam = setups of the exam pool, counted and never read; flaggedTrain = clock-shifted weeks and setups before 2020; unfilled = orders that never filled.

expectedByChance.note: With no real effect anywhere, about 6.2 of the 130 tests would pass discovery (|t| >= 2) and about 0.16 would also confirm with the same sign. The tests overlap, so these are rough.

summary: 130 of 420 pre-registered conditions had enough trades to test. 5 passed discovery; chance alone gives about 6.2.
0 validated, 0 out-of-sample, 2 in-sample only, 3 rejected, 415 inconclusive.

studies.results: The policy took 522 trades at +0.312 R and waited on 954 at +0.219 R: difference +0.093 R, t 0.82, no measurable difference. No reason marks a group of trades that lost money.

table.note: reasons: policyWaits = how often the policy named the reason (eval.json: orders for a gate, the strongest contradicting factor otherwise); trades, share, avg, total, t = all train trades carrying the feature (a proxy, not the policy's own waits).
